entry.title: Welcome — Notes on LLM Systems
entry.content:
Welcome to my personal site. This is where I share my research and engineering notes on large-model systems — distributed training & inference, memory optimization, load scheduling, and heterogeneous hardware.

What I work on

  • Distributed training systems: Megatron-LM / MindSpeed / FlagScale / FSDP pipelines at 1000-GPU scale on Huawei Ascend 910C, MetaX C550, and Ali Zhenwu 810E.
  • Inference systems: vLLM, vLLM-Ascend, SGLang serving and optimization.
  • Memory & scheduling: my current focus — packing strategies, memory-saving operators, and heterogeneous-modeling scheduling for LLM training.

What you will find here

  • Publications — a growing list of papers and preprints, with write-ups.
  • Blog — deeper dives into systems design, lessons from real workloads, and paper notes.
  • Projects — open-source contributions including FlagOS / FlagScale and the zkLLM visualization system.

I am also actively seeking a PhD (2028–2029 Fall) in large-model systems and open to internships in foundation-model, AI-Infra, and robotics teams. If you share similar interests, feel free to reach out via email — 2451427796@qq.com.

entry.title: RAG-Optimized Text-to-Image — Fixing Prompt Mismatch Without Touching the Model

link.title: RAG-Optimized Text-to-Image — Fixing Prompt Mismatch Without Touching the Model

entry.content:
Paper note: “RAG-Optimized Text-to-Image Generation for Consumer Platforms”, published at the WISE 2025 Workshop (Tsinghua BNRist). Code: github.com/Dadada66666/T2I.

The problem

Small-parameter LLMs used as prompt engineers for text-to-image (T2I) systems often fail on implicit knowledge — details that are obvious to a human (subject counts, spatial layout, style expectations) but absent from the user’s short prompt. Rewriting prompts with the LLM alone keeps the gap because the model’s own knowledge is too small to fill it.

Our approach

Instead of modifying the T2I model or retraining anything, we insert a RAG-fronted prompt-optimization stage before the T2I pipeline:

  1. Retrieval: a two-stage hybrid pipeline combining Tavily (web search) with BGE-m3 embeddings in ChromaDB to pull relevant multimodal knowledge for the target scene.
  2. Prompt construction: retrieved context is composed into the rewriting prompt, so the small LLM now “knows” the implicit knowledge it was missing.
  3. Deployment: built on ollama + ComfyUI — one inference pass, no T2I model changes.

Results

Average generation scores improve by +114% over LLM-only rewriting. The framework is model-agnostic: any T2I backend and any small LLM can drop into the pipeline.

Takeaways

  • Prompt engineering is an information problem: give the model the missing knowledge, and its own capacity suffices.
  • RAG works as a pre-processing stage for generation tasks, not only for question answering.
  • Keeping the base models untouched makes the system cheap and portable to consumer-grade hardware.
